scenario: tests/sim_reference_trace.cs: offline Katabatic CTF, no bots; spawn, wait for match start, place the player at (250,-100,terrain+12) with velocity (14,6,0), energy 60; log server-side position | velocity | energy | damage on every change for 8 s.
reference: Original Tribes2.exe (ref/control, no TribesNEXT/QoL) under CrossOver 2026 (Wine) on Rosetta, launched with -nologin.
tribespad: MMU-enforced iPad Simulator build (QoL client), same script.

results.windows -mod Classic run1 vs run2: 7 common states, 0 divergences, identical rest state
results.tribespad run1 vs run2: 8 common states, 0 divergences, identical rest state (266.924 -93.1029 77.1263)
results.windows (no mod) vs tribespad: falling flight bit-identical (4 and 2 common states, 0 divergences); landing velocities identical to every printed digit; positions differ by a constant offset from first ground contact (y -0.0010, z +0.0101); rest 266.924 -93.1019 77.1161 vs 266.924 -93.1029 77.1263

interpretation: Physics integration and the x87 arithmetic it uses match the original game in this scenario. The only difference is the ground-contact position, which QoL changes: its verified collision patch redirects the engine collision query to a community routine that transforms the returned coordinates. The reference here runs without QoL, so this offset is expected but not yet proven to be QoL rather than TribesPad.
also_found: Classic mod (-mod Classic) changes player gravity: vertical speed changes 1.68125 per 62.5 ms sample vs 1.25 without it. TribesPad launches without -mod Classic, matching the original default.
limits: The QoL client does not start under Whisky Wine 7.7 (SDL3.dll video init) or CrossOver (IFC22.dll 0x10032de7), so a QoL-to-QoL comparison is not yet possible on this Mac. One scenario; no weapons, jets, bots or networking.
